subject: general
question: The colour of silver chloride changes when placed in sunlight for some time due to the:

options.text: Photochemical decomposition of silver chloride by sunlight
Combination reaction of silver chloride with oxygen
Displacement reaction by oxygen and water

solution:
The correct answer is __**Photochemical decomposition of silver chloride by sunlight**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Silver chloride** (**AgCl**) is a **white** crystalline solid that is sensitive to light. When it is placed in **sunlight**, it undergoes a **photochemical decomposition** reaction.
 
• The **sunlight** provides the necessary **activation energy** to break the chemical bonds in the **silver chloride** molecule. This results in the formation of **silver metal** and **chlorine gas**.
 
• The **white** color of the salt changes to **grey** due to the accumulation of **metallic silver** particles. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• A **decomposition reaction** is a process where a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances. When this process is triggered by **photons** (light), it is specifically called **photolysis** or **photochemical decomposition**.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is: **2AgCl (s) + Sunlight → 2Ag (s) + Cl2 (g)**. The **chlorine gas** evolved during the process typically escapes into the atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Silver Bromide (AgBr):** Similar to silver chloride, **silver bromide** also undergoes **photochemical decomposition**. It changes from a **pale yellow** color to **grey** when exposed to light.
 
• **Applications in Photography:** These reactions of **silver halides** (silver chloride and silver bromide) were the fundamental basis for **black and white photography**. The light falling on the photographic film would decompose the silver salts to create an image.
 
• **Storage Requirements:** Because of their high sensitivity to light, **silver salts** are always stored in **dark-colored** or **amber-colored bottles**. This prevents **sunlight** from reaching the chemicals and causing premature decomposition.
 
• **Types of Decomposition Reactions:**
 
 
• **Thermal Decomposition:** Triggered by **heat energy** (e.g., heating **calcium carbonate** to get **calcium oxide**).
 
• **Electrolytic Decomposition:** Triggered by **electrical energy** (e.g., **electrolysis of water** to get hydrogen and oxygen).
 
• **Photolytic Decomposition:** Triggered by **light energy** (e.g., decomposition of **AgCl** or **H2O2**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Incorrect Options Analysis:**

 
 
• **Combination reaction:** This involves two substances joining to form one. Silver chloride is breaking down, not combining with oxygen. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Thermal decomposition:** While heat is a form of energy, the specific change in silver chloride color in the presence of **sunlight** is categorized under **photochemical** processes because it responds to the **visible/UV spectrum** of light rather than ambient heat. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Displacement reaction:** This occurs when a more reactive element displaces a less reactive one from its compound. **Oxygen and water** do not displace chlorine from silver chloride in this context. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Observation:** The **grey** color is the most distinct physical evidence of the **chemical change** occurring, indicating that **pure silver** has been liberated from the compound.
